verdict.rationale: Pandoc is a locally installed command-line program and Haskell library. Its first-party docs cover installing it via Homebrew or Chocolatey, a Docker image, a fully self-contained binary, an HTTP server mode (pandoc-server) and running it in GitHub Actions, and community users confirm running it themselves via apt and scripts. missing for 10: explicit evidence of the open-source license or source-build terms, and independent hands-on corroboration of the pandoc-server self-hosted mode.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Pandoc includes a Haskell library and a standalone command-line program.
The resulting binary can be run from any directory and is completely self-contained.
server: compile in support for running in HTTP server mode when the executable is renamed (or symlinked as) pandoc-server.
Alternatively, you can install pandoc using Homebrew: brew install pandoc
The pandoc/latex image also contains the minimal LaTeX installation needed to produce PDFs using pandoc.
